title: Onboarding credit velocity diary
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a personal scratchpad capturing quick experiments for onboarding credits and how they map to token velocity for early users. The goal: design an activation credit that is generous enough to show product value across common flows (chat assistant, codegen, embedding search) but limited so it doesn’t crush unit economics.

High-level constraints / assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- avg GPU blended cost to serve (hosted infra) = $3.00 / GPU-hour (amortized spot+overhead).
- conservative throughput per GPU (mixed models + real convs): ~2M tokens/hour (includes batching, KV cache benefits).
- therefore raw token cost = $3 / 2,000,000 = $0.0000015 per token (i.e., $0.0015 per 1k tokens).
- add infra + product overhead (SLA, telemetry, routing margin) target multiplier = x2.5 => fully loaded cost per 1k tokens = $0.00375.
- target gross margin at scale for starter tier >= 70% => price per 1k tokens target = cost/0.3 = $0.0125 (~$0.013).

Quick unit conversions I use repeatedly:
- 1k tokens ~ 750 words (approx)
- 10 messages in a short chat session ~ 1.5k tokens (mix of short queries + model responses)
- median interactive session in our initial cohort: 600-1,200 tokens

Credit design sketches (variants):
A) Activation bucket (one-time on signup)
- Give 5,000 tokens (~5k credits where 1 credit = 1 token for simplicity)
- Expected sessions unlocked = 4-8 short sessions.
- Cost to us (at baseline fully loaded) = 5 * $0.00375 = $0.01875. Tiny per user.
- Upside: low cost, quick tryout.
- Downside: too small for demos that include codegen or embeddings.

B) Launch trial (time-limited credit pool)
- 30k tokens usable in first 14 days.
- Cost to us = 30 * $0.00375 = $0.1125. Still cheap at scale but shows more value.
- Behavioral hypothesis: 14-day window increases number of high-quality experiments (embedding index builds etc.)

C) Session-first model (bundled sessions)
- Provide 5 "premium" sessions (each session cap = 4k tokens).
- Equivalent tokens = 20k.
- Benefit: easier UX messaging ("5 sessions to try"), easier to cap heavy users.

D) Hybrid credits + rate limit
- 10k tokens + 30 free short sessions (session cap 500 tokens) to encourage many short interactions.
- Aims to nudge users towards interactive flows rather than single large uploads.

Pricing tiers (rough draft numbers):
- Free: 0.02 credits/second? (not precise), but better to show as tokens/month: 5,000 tokens/month + day-zero 2k bonus.
- Starter (self-serve): $20/mo -> included 200k tokens + 10% discount on overage at $0.011/1k tokens.
- Growth: $200/mo -> included 3M tokens + usage-based overage at $0.009/1k tokens.
- Enterprise: custom pricing, SLA, committed capacity.
Note: these are high-level; need to reconcile with Dedicated pricing and Reserved capacity discounts.

Micro-econ thought experiment: cohort A (1000 new signups / month)
- If we give 30k tokens trial to everyone: incremental trial cost = 1000 * $0.1125 = $112.5 / month.
- If 2% convert to Starter at $20/mo = 20 new subs = $400/mo => payback happens quickly.
- Key: conversion lift needs to be >0.5 percentage points to justify bigger trial (very low CAC impact).

Per-session cost sensitivity (approx):
- small interactive session (600 tokens): cost = 0.6 * $0.00375 = $0.00225 per session.
- codegen heavy session (6k tokens): cost = 6 * $0.00375 = $0.0225 per session.
- embedding index build (100k tokens): cost = 100 * $0.00375 = $0.375. Consider charging separately for embedding indexing.

Credit decay / gating heuristics (scratch ideas):
- Tiered decay: activation credits usable only in first 21 days, then convert to 50% discount for next 30 days.
- Guardrails: credits not valid for embedding-builder > 10k tokens unless user provides billing method. Protects against free-index abuse.
- Soft throttles: after X tokens/day from credits, throttle to 10 req/min to prevent bursts that break SLOs.

Behavioral levers (what to test):
- Give credits in small tranches tied to product milestones (create index, first API call, integrate SDK) -> higher chance of retention than one big lump.
- Offer a single large credit for verified org email + credit card on file (higher intent signal).
- Experiment: 30k immediate vs 10k + 3x milestone releases. Track time-to-first-paid-event.

Edge cases and guardrails:
- Fraud: new orgs immediately using embedding-builder to scrape corp data -> require verified billing for > 20k embedding tokens.
- Refund complexity: credits spent should be refundable only as account credit not cash; avoid chargebacks.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a better blended GPU/hour estimate across all regions/instance types (SFO vs FRA vs GCP us-west). TODO: ask infra for recent 90-day blended cost.
- How to incorporate Dedicated contract offsets into free-credit economics? Credits used by a Dedicated account should map to committed capacity, not hosted bottlenecks. Action: map credits to routing tiers.
- UX: how do we show "sessions remaining" when sessions are loosely defined? Might confuse users. Consider "tokens remaining" + a session-length example.
- Track experiments: create Linear tasks and a dashboard to tie trial cohort -> trial usage -> conversion.

Metrics to instrument (minimum):
- activation_credit_used within 14 days (bool)
- avg tokens consumed in first 7 days
- first_paid_event_time (days)
- conversion_rate_by_credit_size
- embedding-builds started from credit pool (event)

Quick experiment matrix (three arms):
- Arm A: 5k day-zero tokens
- Arm B: 30k 14-day tokens
- Arm C: 10k + milestone tranches (2k on signup, 4k after indexing, 4k after first SDK call)
Measure: 30-day conversion, avg tokens/day, support tickets triggered.

Back-of-envelope sensitivity table (fully loaded cost per 1k tokens = $0.00375):
- 1k tokens => $0.0038 cost => price target $0.013 (70% margin)
- 10k tokens => $0.0375 cost => price target ~$0.125
- 100k tokens => $0.375 cost => price target ~$1.25

Notes to self:
- This doc should NOT be shared externally. Lots of rough assumptions.
- Keep this as a living note while we get real cost curves from infra.

Random heuristics I've found helpful when sketching:
- Express experiments both in tokens and in "demoable experiences" (e.g., "build an embedding index of 10 docs = X tokens") because PMs/marketing care about stories not raw tokens.
- Always include a small overage price in the trial policy so power users can continue (and we get conversion signals) rather than outright hard-stop.

End of page.

-- Aisha
